issues.legal_issue: A suit seeking eviction of a tenant from property related to a waqf is within the exclusive jurisdiction of the civil court when the Act does not require the Waqf Tribunal to determine the eviction dispute.
material_facts: The committee brought an eviction suit against a tenant concerning property described as waqf property.
The tenant denied that the property was waqf property and challenged the Waqf Tribunal’s jurisdiction.
The Tribunal initially directed that the plaint be returned to the civil court, then recalled that order because an issue had been framed about whether the property was waqf property.
issues.conclusion: The eviction suit is exclusively triable by the civil court; the Tribunal’s recalled order and the High Court’s decision were set aside, and the order returning the plaint to the civil court was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 6 and 7 of the Waqf Act, 1995 confer Tribunal jurisdiction over specified disputes, including whether property specified in a list of auqaf is waqf property and whether a listed waqf is Shia or Sunni. Sections 83 and 85 do not exclude civil-court jurisdiction for every dispute related to waqf property: under Section 85, jurisdiction is excluded only for matters that the Act requires the Tribunal to determine, and Section 83 does not extend that exclusion. An eviction suit concerning a tenant’s occupation of waqf property is not among the matters assigned to the Tribunal by Sections 6 and 7. The Court followed Ramesh Gobindram (Dead) through LRs v. Sugra Humayun Mirza Wakf, (2010) 8 SCC 726, and held that Bhanwar Lal v. Rajasthan Board of Muslim Wakf, 2013 (11) SCALE 210, was consistent with it; it also noted Board of Wakf, West Bengal v. Anis Fatma Begum, (2010) 14 SCC 588, and Sardar Khan v. Syed Nazmul Hasan, (2007) 10 SCC 727.

predicates.tenant_eviction_suit: A claimant seeks to evict a person alleged to be a tenant from property.
predicates.waqf_related_property: The property in the eviction dispute is described or treated as waqf property.

issues.definition: When a suit seeks to evict a tenant from property described or treated as waqf property, the civil court has exclusive jurisdiction over the eviction suit.
